ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flow-matching action head for a decision-pretrained transformer on continuous control
PROPOSAL: Pretrain an 80M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline trajectories from 40 tasks in Meta-World and the DeepMind Control Suite, replacing the discrete action readout with a conditional flow-matching head that samples actions with 8 integration steps. Training sequences hold a query state and 100 transitions from one task, and the target is the expert action for the query. Evaluate return normalized by expert return on 10 held-out tasks, with the context filled by the agent's own interaction history over 5 episodes, and report how often samples fall near each mode of the expert action distribution.
CONTROLS: Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components, deterministic regression head, and a version prompted with random context to test reliance on context.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The flow head should reach 70 percent of expert return on held-out tasks and beat the mixture head on multi-modal tasks; it may fail if the integration steps push posterior samples toward the mean.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture-density action head tuning for a decision-pretrained transformer on locomotion tasks
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 300M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline trajectories from 12 locomotion tasks in MuJoCo and Brax, using a Gaussian-mixture head trained by negative log-likelihood with mixture sizes of 2, 5 and 10. Training sequences hold a query state and 100 transitions from one task, and the target is the expert action for the query. Use 8 random seeds. Evaluate return normalized by expert return on 6 held-out tasks, with the context filled by the agent's own interaction history over 5 episodes, and report the action log-likelihood on expert data, tabulating both by mixture size.
CONTROLS: Deterministic regression head, a mixture head reduced to a lone component, and a version prompted with random context.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Five components should be enough to capture the locomotion modes, with 10 adding little; the benefit could vanish if the held-out gaits are unimodal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-specific tokenizers for heterogeneous observation and action spaces in a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a 150M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline data from 6 domains, including Meta-World, DeepMind Control Suite and Sinergym building control, with observation and action dimensions between 4 and 120. Compare learned linear tokenizers for every domain that map any observation and action to a shared token of width 512 against a shared tokenizer using zero-filled vectors. Both use a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components. Evaluate normalized return on 8 unseen tasks from these domains, with and without 5 demonstrations in context.
CONTROLS: Zero-filled shared tokenizer, tokenizers trained jointly with a domain-id embedding, and a model trained on one domain only as an anchor.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Domain-specific tokenizers should raise normalized return on unseen tasks by several points over zero-filling, mostly in domains of low dimensionality; the gap may vanish if the transformer infers dimensions from context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenizer design comparison for heterogeneous spaces in a decision-pretrained transformer with four variants
PROPOSAL: Train a 300M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline data from 14 domains, including Meta-World, DeepMind Control Suite, ManiSkill, Brax and Sinergym building control, with observation and action dimensions between 4 and 120. Compare learned linear tokenizers, zero-filled shared tokenizers, a hypernetwork tokenizer that generates the projection from a short domain description, and a set-encoder tokenizer. All use a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components and 3 seeds. Evaluate normalized return on 8 unseen tasks, with and without 5 demonstrations in context, and measure the parameter count of the tokenizers.
CONTROLS: Zero-filled shared tokenizer, tokenizers with a domain-id embedding, a model trained on one domain only as an anchor, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The learned linear tokenizers should match the hypernetwork variant at far lower parameter count, with both beating zero-filling; the set encoder may fail on domains with long observation vectors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Posterior sampling versus greedy action choice when a decision-pretrained transformer adapts online
PROPOSAL: Take a 20M-parameter DPT-style transformer pretrained on offline data from 30 Meta-World tasks with a Gaussian-mixture head of 5 components. On 10 unseen tasks, start with empty context and let it act for 20 episodes, appending its own transitions to the context. Compare sampling actions from the head against taking the mixture mode, and track normalized return after episodes 1, 5 and 20, together with the entropy of the action distribution. Use 5 seeds for the context rollouts and list the tasks where sampling hurts.
CONTROLS: Mode-taking policy, an epsilon-greedy variant of the same model, a random policy, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Sampling should lift return between episodes 1 and 20 more than mode-taking does, as exploration pays off; it may fail if the mixture head is too sharp to explore.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context truncation study for online adaptation of a 300M decision-pretrained transformer on Meta-World
PROPOSAL: Take a 300M-parameter DPT-style transformer pretrained on offline data from 30 Meta-World tasks with a Gaussian-mixture head of 5 components. On 4 unseen tasks, start with empty context and let it act for 20 episodes, with the context truncated to the last 64 or 1024 transitions. Compare normalized return after episodes 1 and 20, together with the entropy of the action distribution, using 10 seeds for the context rollouts, and log the share of rollouts that repeat a failed action sequence once the oldest transitions are dropped.
CONTROLS: Untruncated context, a random policy, an epsilon-greedy variant of the same model, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Longer context should help only after episode 5, since early episodes fit in a short window; the curves could fail to separate if the tasks are solved from the last few transitions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-size scaling of a decision-pretrained transformer on a mixed continuous-control collection
PROPOSAL: Pretrain DPT-style transformers of 20M, 80M and 300M parameters on offline trajectories from 100 tasks spanning Meta-World, the DeepMind Control Suite, Brax and Sinergym, using a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components and a context of 128 transitions. Evaluate normalized return on 20 unseen tasks and 20 parametric variants of training tasks, with context filled online over 10 episodes. Fit a power law of held-out return against parameter count.
CONTROLS: A model trained on a 25 percent subset of the tasks at all three sizes, a behavior-cloning transformer without context, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Return on unseen tasks should rise with size and show diminishing gains, while training-task return saturates early; the power law may fail if the 20M model already reaches the plateau.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dataset-fraction study for an 80M decision-pretrained transformer on mixed continuous control
PROPOSAL: Draw 100 tasks from Meta-World, Brax, Sinergym and the DeepMind Control Suite and pretrain an 80M-parameter DPT-style transformer on their offline trajectories at 4 data fractions with 5 seeds, using a 128-transition context and a 5-component Gaussian-mixture head. Test on 20 unseen tasks and 20 parametric variants of training tasks, filling the context online over 10 episodes, then fit a power law of held-out return against data size.
CONTROLS: A model trained on 25 percent of the tasks with the full trajectories, a behavior-cloning transformer without context, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Held-out return should climb steeply up to 50 percent of the data and flatten after, so the last doubling buys little; the power law might fail if task diversity matters more than trajectory count.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Parametric variants of known environments with demonstration prompting
PROPOSAL: Take an 80M-parameter DPT-style transformer pretrained on offline data from 40 DeepMind Control Suite and Meta-World tasks. Build parametric variants of 6 training environments by scaling gravity, mass and friction by 0.5 and 2, then prompt the model with 5 expert demonstrations collected on the variant, without any online interaction. Measure normalized return and compare it with the same model prompted by demonstrations from the unperturbed environment, to see whether context corrects for the shift. Use 3 seeds for demonstration sampling.
CONTROLS: Unprompted model, a behavior-cloning transformer trained on the same data, and the expert policy on the variant as a ceiling.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Prompting with variant demonstrations should recover most of the lost return, while unperturbed demonstrations do not; it could fail for friction changes that demonstrations barely reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration count study on parametric variants of two locomotion environments
PROPOSAL: Take a 20M-parameter DPT-style transformer pretrained on offline data from 30 DeepMind Control Suite tasks. Build parametric variants of 2 locomotion environments, Walker and Cheetah, by scaling gravity, mass and friction by 0.5 and 2, then prompt the model with 5 or 25 expert demonstrations collected on the variant, without any online interaction. Measure normalized return, sampling the demonstrations 10 times for each count, and relate it to the number of demonstrated transitions that touch the changed parameter.
CONTROLS: Unprompted model, a behavior-cloning transformer trained on the same data, and the expert policy on the variant as a ceiling.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Return should rise with demonstration count and level off by 10 demonstrations; the relation to affected transitions may fail to show if the parameter shifts are mild.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context length for in-context adaptation of a decision-pretrained transformer with sparse attention
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 150M-parameter DPT-style transformers with context windows of 32, 128 and 512 transitions on offline trajectories from 60 tasks in Meta-World, Brax and Sinergym, using sparse attention so that the longest window is affordable and a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components. Evaluate normalized return on 15 unseen tasks with the context filled online over 10 episodes, and with 5 expert demonstrations as the prompt, and report returns by domain.
CONTROLS: Dense attention at the 32 and 128 windows, a model with no context, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Return should improve from 32 to 128 transitions and gain little at 512; sparse attention may fail to keep early transitions that matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Window size comparison for in-context adaptation of a small decision-pretrained transformer on six domains
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 20M-parameter DPT-style transformers with context windows of 128 and 512 transitions on offline trajectories from 60 tasks in Meta-World, Brax, ManiSkill, MuJoCo, Sinergym and the DeepMind Control Suite, using full attention and a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components. Evaluate normalized return on 15 unseen tasks with the context filled online over 10 episodes, and with 5 expert demonstrations as the prompt, with 8 seeds, and break the results down by domain.
CONTROLS: A model with no context, a window of 32 transitions, and the expert policy as a ceiling for comparison.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The longer window should help on domains with long horizons and matter little in the rest; the domain breakdown may fail to show a clear pattern with so few tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Action head comparison with a posterior check on a bandit family with known posterior
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 20M-parameter DPT-style transformers with four action heads, namely diffusion, flow matching, Gaussian mixture with 5 components and 64-bin categorical, on a family of 2000 synthetic continuous-action bandits whose Bayesian posterior over the best action is computable. Compare the head distributions with the exact posterior by Wasserstein distance as the context grows from 1 to 50 observations. Then run the best 2 heads on 30 Meta-World tasks and compare normalized return on 10 held-out tasks, with context filled online over 5 episodes.
CONTROLS: Exact posterior sampling as the reference, a deterministic regression head, and a uniform random head as a floor.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Diffusion and flow heads should track the exact posterior closely, while the categorical head loses accuracy in fine detail; the best heads may fail to transfer their advantage to the control tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixture-count sensitivity of the Gaussian-mixture head on synthetic bandits and four control domains
PROPOSAL: Pretrain 150M-parameter DPT-style transformers with a Gaussian-mixture head with 2, 5, 10 and 20 components on a family of 5000 synthetic continuous-action bandits whose Bayesian posterior is computable. Compare the head distributions with the exact posterior by Wasserstein distance as the context grows from 1 to 100 observations, with 8 seeds. Then evaluate the same models on 40 tasks from Meta-World, Brax, Sinergym and MuJoCo, comparing normalized return on 10 held-out tasks, and report how the gap changes with the number of components.
CONTROLS: Exact posterior sampling as the reference, a deterministic regression head, and a uniform random head as a floor.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Five components should come close to the exact posterior with 10 and 20 adding little; the held-out control gap between counts may fail to appear.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Expert demonstration prompting against a retrieval baseline for a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: Prompt an 80M-parameter DPT-style transformer, pretrained on offline data from 50 tasks, with 5 expert demonstrations on 12 unseen tasks from Meta-World and Brax, and compare normalized return with a transformer trained by behavior cloning that retrieves the 5 nearest demonstrations by state similarity. Test whether the DPT-style model improves on retrieval as the demonstrations get noisier, by adding action noise to the demonstrations at three levels.
CONTROLS: Behavior-cloning transformer with retrieval, the same DPT-style model without demonstrations, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The DPT-style model should beat retrieval when demonstrations are noisy, since it infers the task rather than copying actions; the edge may fail if retrieval already matches the task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Demonstration quantity and quality study for a decision-pretrained transformer on control domains
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 300M-parameter DPT-style transformer on 50 tasks, then supply 5, 10 or 20 expert demonstrations for 12 unseen tasks from Meta-World, Brax and MuJoCo. Score normalized return against a behavior-cloning transformer that retrieves the nearest demonstrations by state similarity, and add action noise to the demonstrations at three levels with 5 draws of demonstrations, plotting return against noise level.
CONTROLS: Behavior-cloning transformer with retrieval, the same DPT-style model without demonstrations, and the expert policy as a ceiling for comparison.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Return should saturate near 10 demonstrations and the DPT-style model should beat retrieval under noise; the plots could fail to separate the two models at mild noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-domain observation normalization for a decision-pretrained transformer
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 20M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline data from 6 domains in Meta-World, Brax and Sinergym, comparing running mean and standard deviation normalization computed separately for the domains with rank normalization and no normalization. Use a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components. Evaluate normalized return on 8 unseen tasks with context filled online over 5 episodes. Report the steps to reach 80 percent of final return.
CONTROLS: No normalization, a single normalizer computed on pooled data, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Separate statistics should help the most on domains with large differences in scale of observations; the effect may fail to show if the encoder learns its own scaling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Observation normalization study for a 150M decision-pretrained transformer on twelve domains
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 150M-parameter DPT-style transformer on offline data from 12 domains in Meta-World, Brax, Sinergym, ManiSkill and MuJoCo, comparing running mean and standard deviation normalization with rank normalization and no normalization, using 3 seeds. Use a Gaussian-mixture head with 5 components. Evaluate normalized return on 20 unseen tasks with context filled online over 10 episodes, and plot the gap against the spread of observation scales.
CONTROLS: No normalization, a normalizer computed on pooled data, and the expert policy as a ceiling for comparison.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Rank normalization should be as good as running statistics and more stable on heavy-tailed observations; the plot may fail to show a trend if scale spread is similar between domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-domain flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer against large action model baselines
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a 300M-parameter DPT-style transformer with a flow-matching action head on offline trajectories from 200 tasks in 8 domain families, including Meta-World, DeepMind Control Suite, Brax, ManiSkill, Sinergym and industrial process control, using domain-specific tokenizers. Evaluate normalized return on 30 unseen tasks and 30 parametric variants of training tasks in two regimes: empty context filled online over 20 episodes, and a prompt of 5 expert demonstrations. Compare with Gato-style and Algorithm Distillation models of the same size trained on the same data.
CONTROLS: Gato-style transformer, Algorithm Distillation transformer trained on the same trajectories, the same model with a mixture head, and the expert policy as a ceiling.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The flow-matching model should beat both baselines on unseen tasks in each regime, with the largest gap in the online regime; it may fail on the process-control tasks, whose dynamics differ most from the rest.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-scale flow-matching decision-pretrained transformer on three domains with repeated training
PROPOSAL: Using 60 tasks from Meta-World, the DeepMind Control Suite and Brax, train an 80M-parameter DPT-style transformer whose action head is conditional flow matching, with per-domain tokenizers and 8 training seeds. Report normalized return on 12 unseen tasks and 12 parametric variants of training tasks under two protocols: empty context filled online over 20 episodes, and a prompt of 5 expert demonstrations. Gato-style and Algorithm Distillation models of matching size serve as comparisons, trained on the same trajectories with the same tokenizers.
CONTROLS: Gato-style model, Algorithm Distillation model on the same trajectories, a mixture-head version of the transformer, and the expert policy as ceiling.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Expect the flow-matching model to lead both baselines on unseen tasks, most clearly in the online protocol; the spread between seeds may fail to stay small on Brax tasks.
